name: How Do You Know If a Kitchen Remodel Needs Structural Changes?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my kitchen remodel needs structural changes?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if my kitchen remodel needs structural changes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Structural changes are needed when the remodel goes beyond finishes and into the building itself. Common triggers include removing a wall, widening a doorway, adding a pass-through, changing window openings, or correcting damage in framing or subflooring. In older Los Angeles County homes, you may not know whether a wall is load-bearing until the structure is reviewed carefully. That is why wall removal should never be treated as a simple cosmetic choice. A proper assessment will determine whether support beams, posts, or redesign of adjacent areas are needed. If your goal is to improve flow, the contractor should confirm what can be changed safely and what will require additional engineering or permit review before demolition begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Your kitchen likely needs structural changes if you want to remove load-bearing walls, enlarge openings, add windows or doors, or correct major framing problems. A contractor or structural professional should review the space before any wall removal or major layout change begins.
